findings.summary: Spec requirement 3 is not delivered: the ordering validation that raises the reported ORDER_VIOLATION lives in the pinned plugin's generation-unaware check_chain_order, run over the committed feedback index at review seal; the change only makes the engine-side mirror consulted by the replayer generation-aware, so a valid later generation's continuous_review materialization still fails with the identical error.

Spec requirements 4 and 6 are not met: the cross-generation regression asserts pipeline completion against the Sealer() test double (tests/test_dd_pipeline.py:63), which performs no ordering validation, so it proves only that the replayer did not decline the replay -- not that the current generation's continuous review materializes, and not any structured materialization result from a materializer that enforces the ordering rule.

The generation-aware mirror now diverges from the carrier it documents itself as mirroring, converting a deliberate fail-closed refusal into 'trim the tree to the sealed tip, then fail at the carrier' -- exactly the outcome the surrounding comment says it fail-closes to prevent.

Spec requirement 5's refusal regression proves only that the replayer declines to replay a partial prefix; the run then proceeds through every stage to TERMINAL_COMPLETE, so no test proves that a genuinely invalid same-chain new attempt lacking its prior REJECT is still rejected at materialization.

Product consistency between the implement and review commits was not verified mechanically: the reviewer has read-only file inspection and no shell or Git in this worktree, so the required exclude-.dev-dispatch diff was not executed. Only .dev-dispatch/ review artifacts and the feedback index were observed, which is consistent with a metadata-only materialization but does not establish it.

The sealed implement handoff records work_head_commit 4417064912280eb7136fa2dffda2844ca62f3442, while the dispatch context names 4da170e1566adbc2e952901384204619d0fdf8c9 as the product commit; this is consistent with a metadata-only seal stacked on the product commit, but the two identities are not interchangeable.
